verdicts.strongest_argument: Every number in this claim comes from the single most-scrutinised earnings release on the tape. Meta's Q2 2026 press release (2026-07-29) states ad impressions +14% and average price per ad +12%; Meta's Q1 2026 release (2026-04-29) states +19% and +12%. Both are verified, both are public, and the specific observation that price-per-ad printed +12% for a second consecutive quarter has already been written up in ad-industry trade press (digitalapplied, 'Meta Ads After Q2: Planning for +12% Price Per Ad'). More important, the mechanism is misspecified. ODDITY's own 20-F and the June 2 call attribute the CPA blow-up to its largest partner down-weighting the 'Try Before You Buy' model because of high return rates -- an attribution/eligibility problem specific to ODDITY -- not to blended auction price inflation. Meta's +12% blended price per ad is roughly its normal run-rate and says almost nothing about whether TBYB traffic has been re-weighted. Meta-attributed orders are 'just under a quarter' of ODDITY revenue (ppc.land, from the company's own disclosure), so even a full read-across is a quarter-weight input. And ODDITY has already given the market a far more direct datum than Meta's blended pricing: on 2026-06-02 it disclosed IL MAKIAGE CPA down 28% sequentially in May, i.e. inside Meta's Q2 and after it. The residual novelty here is a framing of the consensus bear thesis that Jefferies, Goldman and KeyBanc have all published since February.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Meta Q2 2026: ad impressions +14% y/y, average price per ad +12% y/y.
Meta Q1 2026: ad impressions +19% y/y, average price per ad +12% y/y -- the comparison base the finding uses.
Trade-press write-up of exactly the '+12% price per ad, unchanged from Q1' observation.
Identifies Meta as ODDITY's largest advertising partner, quantifies it at just under a quarter of revenue, and attributes the CPA spike to TBYB being down-weighted after an algorithm change.
Company discloses May IL MAKIAGE CPA down 28% sequentially and the 40% shift of acquisition revenue from TBYB to standard Buy -- a more direct Q2 read than Meta's blended pricing.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No move in ODD around 2026-07-29 is identifiable in the baseline; the 20-day run-up is +5.13% and the 5-day is -7.43%, i.e. the fade is recent and post-dates Meta's print by five weeks. The absence of a reaction is as consistent with 'the market does not think Meta's blended pricing reads across' as with 'the market missed it'.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence tying ODDITY's CPA specifically to auction clearing price rather than to TBYB eligibility -- e.g. company disclosure that the fix depends on Meta CPM levels rather than on model re-weighting.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every figure in this claim -- 24,001 contracts, 99.9% of the day's volume, 2.8x the 8,509 pre-existing open interest, the $14.54 spot, and the 90/110 three-month skew falling 4.76 points to 0.73 -- is stated verbatim in the investing.com article the hunter cites, published 2026-09-03, six days before the print. That is wire copy, and it is the definition of published. The one element that is the hunter's own is the inference that a falling skew alongside a 24k-lot put print means size was sold to dealers rather than bought, which the article explicitly declines to draw (it calls the flow 'defensive positioning' and 'tail-risk hedging'). On the merits, the hunter's inference is the better-supported one and I concede that much: if 24k deep-OTM puts had been bought, 90/110 skew would have risen, not fallen 4.76 points on the same session. But the tradeable content is very small. The premium involved is on the order of $0.5-1.0m against a $615m market cap, a $7.50 October strike 48% below spot is a lottery-ticket line whose print says nothing about the sign of a September 9 result, and the stock has already fallen 8.3% from the $14.54 quoted in the article to today's $13.33 -- so whatever information the flow carried has had five sessions to be absorbed.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Reports the 24,001-lot October $7.50 put block, 99.9% of volume, 2.8x the 8,509 open interest, and the 90/110 skew falling 4.76 points to 0.73 -- all of the finding's numbers.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Spot has fallen from the article's $14.54 on 2026-09-03 to 13.33 on 2026-09-08 (run_up_5d_pct -7.43), so the tape moved after the flow was published. The baseline's front-expiry skew of -16.19 vol points (calls bid over puts) is directionally consistent with put-side supply, but with total_open_interest of only 945 contracts and an ATM bid-ask of 41.5% of mid, that skew number is close to unmeasurable and should not be leaned on by either hunter.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Trade-side identification (e.g. an exchange time-and-sales print showing the block on the bid) confirming the direction, plus evidence the block was not one leg of a spread, collar or roll.

verdicts.strongest_argument: I checked all eight filings against EDGAR CIK 0001907085 and the headline conclusion is correct: only 2026-02-25 (FY2025 results, filed 07:06 UTC, exhibit 99-1) and 2026-06-02 (Q1 2026 results, 'issued a press release announcing financial results for the first quarter ended March 31, 2026') are earnings. But two of the enumerations are wrong. 2026-06-12 is NOT the AGM proxy statement -- it is the Oddity Finance exchangeable-note repurchase 6-K, the very document the other hunter builds ODD-b#2 on; the proxy statement and proxy card are 2026-06-16 (Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2, AGM of 2026-07-29). And 2026-01-12 is not addressed at all: it is the $350m credit-facility amendment 6-K. So the arithmetic 'two of eight' survives, but the working does not. On pricing: the facts themselves are about as public as facts get. ODD fell 49% on 2026-02-25 and ~30% on 2026-06-02; Calcalist, Reuters and every wire covered the February crash, Jefferies cut its target 72% from $64 to $18 that week, and the -79%-from-52-week-high in the baseline is the market's own record of it. The market does not need telling that ODD's last two earnings were catastrophic. What is genuinely new here is a correction to OUR sealed baseline file, not to the market's information set. The derived implication -- that a 20.74% implied move understates a 49%/30% history -- also rests on a three-day straddle with a 41.5% bid-ask on 945 contracts of open interest, so the 'only 20.7% is priced' half of the comparison is not a reliable statement of what the market pays, and two crisis prints where guidance collapsed from a standing start is not a base rate for a third print where guidance is already reset to -25/-30% and the stock is already down 79%.

prior_publication.what_it_says: 6-K filed 07:06 UTC with a 197KB Exhibit 99-1 -- the FY2025 results release behind the -49.21% move.
'On June 2, 2026, ODDITY Tech Ltd. issued a press release announcing financial results for the first quarter ended March 31, 2026.'
REFUTES the finding's characterisation of 06-12: this filing is the $50m note repurchase, not a proxy statement.
Credit-facility amendments to $350m -- an eighth filing the finding does not account for, also not earnings.
Front-page coverage of the ~50% crash on the algorithm-error revenue warning -- the reaction the finding says is unknown is one of the year's better-covered blow-ups.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The baseline itself already carries the correction in substance: event_plausibility.cadence_implausible is true, and the reason field states outright that 'the 8 matched filings are not earnings' and 'the reaction history above should not be used as an earnings base rate'. The finding upgrades an already-flagged defect from 'unusable' to 'two usable observations' -- real value to the pipeline, near-zero value to the market.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A tradeable implied-move quote from a liquid expiry (not a 3-DTE line with a 41.5% spread) showing the market genuinely pays materially less than 30%.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is the one finding where I mostly concede the novelty and can only argue the mechanism. The dates check out against primary sources: Q1 2025 on 2025-04-29 and Q2 2025 on 2025-08-04 (both 6-Ks on EDGAR; the Q2 2025 advisory confirms 'after the market close on Monday, August 4' with the call the next morning), against Q1 2026 on 2026-06-02 and Q2 2026 on 2026-09-09 pre-open with a same-morning 08:30 ET call. That is +34 and +36 days, with FY unchanged at February 25 in both years, exactly as claimed. Each individual date is in a public press release, so nothing here is hidden -- but I could find no publication drawing the year-on-year delta, so this sits in the 'public but nobody has done the subtraction' band rather than lower. What I do dispute is the implication. ODDITY is an Israeli foreign private issuer: it has no SEC quarterly filing deadline at all, only the annual 20-F, so slipping interim dates is costless and carries none of the signalling a domestic issuer's 10-Q delay would. The FY date being untouched is consistent with that -- the only deadline-bound report did not move. And the direction is ambiguous even if the delay is deliberate: reporting Q2 seventy days after quarter end means management has two extra months of Q3 CPA data when it guides, which is as likely to enable a credible recovery narrative as to conceal a bad one.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Q2 2025 results after market close 2025-08-04 with the call the following morning -- the prior-year comparison the finding uses.
Q2 2026 results before market open 2026-09-09 with the call at 08:30 ET the same morning -- both halves of the schedule change are in this release.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: None. There is no identifiable move in the tape around 2026-07-22 when the Q2 2026 date was announced, and the baseline's 20-day window does not reach it.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A company or auditor statement giving a benign operational reason for the interim shift, or conversely any disclosure of a review, restatement or control issue that would make the delay diagnostic.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The series is free, public and on the exact URL cited, and alt-data desks have watched ilmakiage.com since the February crash -- but the numbers as reported do not reconcile, and the evidentiary weight is low even where they do. Fetching the cited Semrush page today returns May 2.51M, June 2.44M, July 2.36M visits and a global rank of 23,439 -- not the 10,747-to-15,447 slide the finding reports. The 15,447 figure appears on Similarweb attached to an April 2026 page, so the rank series here is conflated across two providers and at least one wrong month. There is no August figure on the cited Semrush page at all; the '~2.3M in August (-4.73%)' is the hunter's extrapolation presented alongside measured months. And the 28.84% Display share of desktop visits is behind Semrush's paywall -- the free page shows Direct 42.18% and Google 14.1% and no channel split -- so the load-bearing premise that this is 'a direct read on the paid-acquisition funnel' is not verifiable from the source given. On weight: Semrush and Similarweb are panel-modelled, not measured, and month-over-month deltas of 3-5% on a 2.4M-visit site are inside both the model error and ordinary summer seasonality for colour cosmetics. Most damaging of all, the sign may be backwards. The company has already guided Q2 revenue down 25-30% year on year. A site drifting down 3% a month sequentially is not evidence that guide is being missed; if anything it is consistent with, or better than, a guide of that severity.

prior_publication.what_it_says: The cited page itself, free and public: May 2.51M, June 2.44M, July 2.36M visits, global rank 23,439, no August data and no channel split without an account.
Similarweb shows ilmakiage.com at global rank ~15,447 for April 2026 -- the figure the finding presents as the August endpoint of a three-month slide.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No datable tape reaction, because a continuously-updated third-party page has no publication date to trade against. The 5-day fade of -7.43% is better explained by the 2026-09-03 options story and pre-print de-risking than by a traffic series with no news event.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A verifiable, single-provider, same-methodology series showing a break in trend -- a double-digit sequential drop, or a year-on-year decline materially worse than the -25/-30% already guided.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The share count is right and I verified it independently on two sites, which is precisely the problem: 6,583,805 shares short against 5,998,488 the prior settlement is published on stockanalysis.com, MarketBeat, Fintel, Nasdaq and Benzinga, and it is the FINRA 2026-08-14 settlement, disseminated around 2026-08-26. Twelve days before the print, on every free retail terminal, is not information. Two qualifications. First, the '23% of float' is denominator-dependent: stockanalysis reaches it on a 28.57M Class A float, MarketBeat publishes 11.43% on a wider base for the identical share count. The borrow-relevant number is arguably the Class A one, but the headline percentage is contestable rather than a fact. Second, 'shorts added into the rally and into the print' over-reads a series that stops on 2026-08-14: it says nothing about the last three and a half weeks, during which the stock has fallen 7.4% in five sessions. Third and most important, the skew reinterpretation is refuted by the other hunter's evidence on the same tape. The claim is that the -16.19 vol-point skew is a crowded short book buying OTM calls as gap protection. On 2026-09-03, the day the skew inverted, ODD traded 24,012 puts against four calls. There was no call buying. The mechanical cause of calls being bid relative to puts was put-side supply, not call-side demand -- and independently, with total front-expiry open interest of 945 contracts and an ATM bid-ask of 41.5% of mid, that skew reading is not measurable enough to sustain either story.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Short interest 6.58M, previous month 6.00M, 23.04% of a 28.57M float, short ratio 8.96 -- exactly the finding's figures, free and public.

Settlement 2026-08-14: 6,583,805 shares short, +9.8% from 5,998,488 on 7/31, days to cover 8.74 -- same share count, but 11.43% of float on a wider denominator, and it dates the data three and a half weeks before the print.
24,012 puts versus 4 calls traded on the day the skew moved -- contradicts the finding's reading of the skew as short-book call buying.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The baseline's skew_25d_vol_points of -16.19 and priced_direction_lean 'upside paid' is the object of the reinterpretation, but it is computed on the 2026-09-11 expiry with total_open_interest of 945 and atm_spread_frac_of_mid of 0.415. That is not a book from which a 16-vol-point wing differential can be extracted with confidence in either direction. Squeeze risk is real and structural, and the 8.7-8.9 day cover is unchanged in character from June.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A post-2026-08-14 settlement showing shorts still adding through the September fade, or call-side volume and open-interest data supporting the hedging story that the 2026-09-03 flow contradicts.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The transaction is correctly described -- I read the 6-K and it says $50m face of the 0% Exchangeable Senior Notes due 2030 repurchased for $35m, closing 2026-06-17, $550m remaining -- and it does land inside Q2. It is also correctly noted that a gain on extinguishment sits in GAAP and not in the $0.1223 adjusted consensus, so it cannot mechanically produce an adjusted beat. But this was filed on EDGAR on 2026-06-12 and picked up the same day by TipRanks, GuruFocus and StockTitan, and ODD closed +6.93% that session. That is publication plus a visible tape reaction on the day the information arrived, which is the strongest form of 'priced'. What remains unpublished is only the arithmetic step -- roughly $14-15m pre-tax gain, given ASU 2020-06 leaves the notes carried near face less unamortised issuance cost -- and that step is mechanical enough that any analyst carrying a GAAP line already has it. The credit inference is the weaker half. A 0% coupon note due 2030 whose conversion option is worthless with the stock down 79% is a pure-discount instrument; 70 cents over roughly four years is a ~9% yield, which is high-yield pricing, not distress, and most of the discount is arithmetic rather than credit. The company drew $350m of amended facilities in January and has been buying back stock under a $200m authorisation. The realistic effect on 2026-09-09 is a possible headline-versus-adjusted EPS confusion in the first minutes of the tape.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Oddity Finance LLC agreed 2026-06-11 to repurchase $50m face of the 0% Exchangeable Notes due 2030 for $35m, closing 2026-06-17, leaving $550m outstanding.
Wire pick-up of the same 6-K, headlined explicitly on the discount.
Second same-day pick-up of the note repurchase.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: The baseline records +6.93% on 2026-06-12, the filing date. The market saw this document and repriced on it. That move is in the history list the other hunter (ODD-a#2) correctly identifies as non-earnings -- which is exactly why it is usable here as a clean single-catalyst reaction.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Confirmation that sell-side GAAP models exclude the extinguishment gain, so that a reported GAAP EPS well above published GAAP estimates would surprise the tape on the morning.

interactions: Three overlaps, one of them a direct contradiction. (1) ODD-a#2 and ODD-b#2 rest on the SAME EDGAR document set and disagree about one of its members: a#2 characterises the 2026-06-12 6-K as the AGM proxy statement, b#2 characterises it as the Oddity Finance note repurchase. I fetched tm2617509d1_6k.htm and b#2 is right -- 06-12 is the note repurchase; the proxy statement and proxy card are 06-16 (Exhibits 99.1/99.2). a#2's conclusion 'only two of eight are earnings' nonetheless survives, because 06-12 is not earnings either, but a#2 also silently omits 2026-01-12, which is the $350m credit-facility amendment. Judges downstream should take a#2's conclusion and b#2's document identification, not a#2's enumeration. (2) ODD-a#1 and ODD-b#1 read the SAME options evidence -- the 2026-09-03 investing.com piece on the 24,001-lot October $7.50 put block -- in opposite directions, and the data supports a#1. If 24k deep-OTM puts had been bought, three-month 90/110 skew would have risen; it fell 4.76 points to 0.73 that session, which is put-side supply. b#1's story requires call-side demand from a crowded short book, and there were four call contracts traded against 24,012 puts that day. There was no call buying to hedge with. Separately, both hunters lean on the baseline's -16.19 25-delta skew, and neither should: it is computed on a 2026-09-11 expiry with 945 total contracts of open interest and a 41.5%-of-mid ATM spread, which cannot support a 16-vol-point wing inference in either direction. The honest statement is that ODD's front-week option book is too thin to say what direction the market has paid for, and by extension the baseline's 20.74% implied move and 'upside paid' lean should both be treated as indicative only, as the file's own warning says. (3) ODD-a#0 and ODD-b#0 are two attempts at the same unobservable -- whether the paid-acquisition funnel recovered in Q2. a#0 proxies it with Meta's blended price per ad, b#0 with modelled ilmakiage.com visits. Both are weak proxies for a problem the company itself has described as TBYB down-weighting, and the company gave a more direct number than either on 2026-06-02 (May CPA -28% sequentially). They should not be scored as two independent pieces of evidence pointing the same way.
